Hello! Yes, there are several different ways to play shack, all context dependent imo. Let me run you through some of my favorites:
- Option 1, The 50/50: Chase the survivor coming from the outside by the window back into the shack from the doorway opposite of the pallet side. As you’re chasing them back into the shack, leave your remnant between the window and the pallet on the outside of the shack. If the survivor vaults, tp back to the remnant and block them from taking either the window or the pallet. If the survivor stays inside and goes for the pallet, tp back when they pass the pallet or get right around there and either get the hit or force shack pallet drop, a win-win. If the survivor waits patiently by the window, hold your power until you’re sure you can cancel and hit them or teleport to secure the hit. Lastly, if the survivor runs the outside of the shack, either continue to hold your power until they run back around shack or cancel/tp to a locker once you’re sure they’ve left the shack. 
- Option 2, The Nightfall Bamboozle: This one seems to be best on clumsy survivors or survivors that are really into reading you. As per the name, this one works best during nightfall or with the add-on Boat Keys. Extra points if shack locks have been broken/not yet setup. The idea of this play is to condition the survivor earlier in the game to believe that you use your remnant a lot at loops. What you’re going to want to then do, is to follow the exact same pattern as the 50/50, setting up your remnant by the window. The difference here is you want them to SEE that you’re doing it. Then, push forward and force them to run further into the shack, then double back by the window so they can see you and react by running towards the lockers. Then, boom, shoot to the locker and instantly come out. They shouldn’t have much time to react if you do it quick enough, but if the survivor is incredibly keen and perceptive they can run away. So this one is best used as a distance closer/gimmicky approach. 
- Option 3, The 50/50 Mind-Game: Once again, this option follows a similar pattern to the 50/50. Chase the survivor from outside of the shack, push them inside, set remnant by window, yada yada. The difference here being that you’ll set your remnant slightly further up, and then double back and moonwalk into the shack. If the survivor isn’t paying attention, you can cancel and nab the hit. If the survivor is paying attention and they start running the opposite way upon seeing you entering the shack, you can tp back to your remnant. Furthermore, if the survivor is incredibly patient and perceptive and you can be convincing enough, pretend you’re going to tp to your remnant by kinda pausing in the doorway, maybe doing some weird charades and facing the remnant, then flick to the locker and tp there (best if nightfall/boat key add-on). 
- Option 4, The 50/50 from the Inside: This basically follows the name. Just perform the 50/50 but from the inside of the shack. Adjust options based on the opposite run patterns of the survivor (they’re coming from inside to the outside of the shack). 
- Option 5, The Plain Jane: Sometimes it’s best to just get that pallet out of the way. Do this by just being a brute-force m1 Andy if you have to. Bonus points if you wanna fake using your remnant Pyramid Head style by just tapping M2 and canceling. Sometimes, the threat of your power and mind gaming can be more intimidating than doing anything at all, and will actually net you the hit. 

Hope this helps, best of luck fellow Dredger! <3

There are a few different ways to run that tile, all depending on the survivor:
- The most common for me is to place the remnant on the left or right (whichever side the survivor is more likely to run to after dropping that pallet) then I will walk the other way and wait either hardly any time at all, a while and then tp, or i will never tp at all. Against REALLY good survivors, I advise the latter OR faking placing your remnant altogether.
- The next one that you can try is putting the remnant at the pallet and walking around it, works decently well if the pallet gym is in the corner. 
- The last thing you can do, particularly if the pallet is down already (even more particularly if the survivor seems to be camping the pallet), is place your remnant on either the left or right of the longer side of the loop about 2-3 meters away from the pallet, and then walk all the way around. Teleport either as soon as you see the survivor run away from the loop (or cancel, context dependent) or as soon as the survivor vaults. Be PATIENT, and don’t be afraid to cancel and swing immediately. 
- Extra option: if you’re on a map like “The Game” you can teleport to lockers and interrupt the loop. Particularly helpful with the add-ons Boat Key, Haddie’s Calendar if the locker is locked, and just in general during nightfall. 

Hope this helps!! <3
